title: Staging-only feature flag for new provision-to-ready pipeline (v2)
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes:
- Adds a staging-only gate for provisioning pipeline v2 so we can pilot safely without impacting prod pool expansions.
- Adds dashboards/metrics checklist and runbook links in the operator docs for the pilot rollout.
description: Context: We’re rolling out the new provision-to-ready automation (v2) behind a safe gate so we can pilot on internal pools and a single customer expansion without risk of accidentally enabling in production. This PR adds a staging-only feature flag that controls whether the control plane will accept v2 provisioning runs and whether the routing/control-plane “Ready” transitions use v2 semantics. Design: (1) Introduce a single flag `provisioning.pipeline_v2.enabled` in control-plane config with a hard environment guard: the flag is only honored when `DEPLOY_ENV=staging` (or equivalent cluster env). In prod, the flag is forced off and any attempt to enable is logged and ignored. (2) Expose the effective value via `/internal/config` and include it in provisioning run metadata for audit/debug. (3) Add guardrails at API boundaries: the “trigger provisioning run” endpoint will reject `pipelineVersion=v2` unless the effective flag is enabled. Rollout plan: Step 0: merge and deploy to staging only. Step 1: enable flag in staging control-plane config; run v2 on one internal staging pool (ENG-2752). Step 2: monitor the metrics listed below for 24h, then proceed to a small prod pilot using the existing v1 pipeline (prod remains unaffected by this flag). Step 3: after staging confidence, we will add a separate production rollout mechanism (not in scope here) that will require explicit approval + change window. Metrics to monitor (staging): `fleet_provisioning_run_total{pipeline_version="v2"}`, `fleet_provisioning_stage_duration_seconds{stage=...}`, `fleet_provisioning_run_failed_total{reason=...}`, `fleet_provisioning_time_to_ready_seconds` (p50/p95), `control_plane_ready_transition_total{from=...,to=...}`, and the stuck-stage alerts in the Dedicated Readiness dashboard. Notes: This flag is intentionally boring and central; we want a single switch + env gate, not multiple ad-hoc toggles. Follow-ups: ENG-2753 (customer pilot comms + rollback), ENG-2751 (pause/resume controls), and dashboards tuning once we see real staging traffic. References: Confluence overview + ADR-0142/ADR-0143 (orchestration model and validation gates).
commits: control-plane: add provisioning pipeline v2 feature-flag plumbing
control-plane: enforce staging-only environment guard + warning logs
api: reject v2 provisioning trigger when flag disabled; include effective flag in response metadata
telemetry: tag provisioning counters/histograms with pipeline_version (bounded cardinality)
docs: add staging rollout checklist + metrics links for v2 pilot

Added a runbook section with the exact config knob, verification endpoint, and a revert step. Rafael Mendes: Please ensure the rejection behavior is clear to operators when they try to trigger v2 while disabled; they should get a useful error and a pointer to the runbook. Connor O'Brien (author): Updated the API error to `409 ProvisioningPipelineDisabled` with message including `effective=false`, `env=prod|staging`, and a link to the runbook doc path. Also tagged the metric `fleet_provisioning_run_rejected_total{reason="pipeline_disabled"}`. Ethan Park: How are we preventing cardinality blowups with `pipeline_version` labels? Also can we expose the effective flag in the run status output for debugging? Connor O'Brien (author): `pipeline_version` is an enum (v1/v2) and the labels are constrained. Added `effectivePipelineVersion` and `pipelineV2EnabledEffective` to the run status payload and persisted it in the run record. Allison Grant: Please add a short metrics checklist to the doc and link to the readiness dashboard spec so folks know what to watch.
